messages:
maya (support): FYI customer (Acme) opened a P1 — they say some audit events are missing in their SIEM after we enabled the 90d retention export. They see gaps for service_start/service_stop events from last week. examples: event_ids: `evt_8a3f1`, `evt_8a3f2` :eyes:

claire (support): Do they mean missing from the S3 export or missing downstream in Splunk? Any error messages on their side?

accts (via maya): They pasted Splunk ingest errors: `schema_mismatch: field actor_id not found` and also `403: kms: decrypt failed` for a handful of objects. They think it started around 2026-03-05.

maya (support): Attaching their snippet of the Splunk error and our export job id: `export-job-20260305-42`.

audits-bot: export-job-20260305-42 status: COMPLETED, objects: 312, failures: 4, s3_prefix: `s3://redwood-audit-prod/exports/2026-03-05/`

jason (eng-security): OK first pass — two likely separate issues: 1) schema/field name drift between agent versions (actor.id vs actor_id) causing Splunk props to reject events; 2) KMS-encrypted objects that the SIEM can't decrypt because we rotated key labels and the export metadata didn't include kms_key_id.

emily (infra): We rolled a pipeline change on 2026-03-04: audit-exporter v2.3.1 normalized event keys to camelCase (`actorId`/`serviceStart`) and enabled `strip_sensitive=true` by default. That would explain actor_id -> actorId mapping and removal of some nested fields. The export job log shows 4 objects skipped due to kms metadata missing.

nate (sre): Can we reproduce fetch for the customer's timeframe? maya, can you share the sample event ids (I only have `evt_8a3f1/2`), and customer org id? Also need the export manifest: `s3://redwood-audit-prod/exports/2026-03-05/manifest.json`

maya (support): Org id `org-acme-77`. Here are two sample event ids they gave: `evt_8a3f1`, `evt_8a3f2`. Sending manifest link privately.

jason (eng-security): Quick repro steps for SRE/infra:
1) curl our internal audit API to retrieve raw events for org `org-acme-77` around `2026-03-04..2026-03-06`:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://internal-api.redwood/1/audit/events?org=org-acme-77&start=2026-03-04T00:00:00Z&end=2026-03-06T23:59:59Z&limit=1000" | jq '.data[] | select(.id=="evt_8a3f1" or .id=="evt_8a3f2")'
```
2) compare keys in raw event vs exported object in S3: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit-prod/exports/2026-03-05/part-0003.gz - | gunzip | jq 'select(.id=="evt_8a3f1")'`
3) check export job log for kms errors: `grep -E "decrypt|kms" /var/log/audit-exporter/2026-03-05.log`

claire (support): I ran step 1 for event `evt_8a3f1` — raw event has `actor: { id: "u-333", email: "sre@acme.com" }` (camelCase). Exported object (from S3) shows `actor_id: "u-333"` for many events but not consistently. Some files have `actorId`. So looks like mixed versions in export batches.

emily (infra): That matches: we had two exporter instances rolling (old v2.2.0 + new v2.3.1) during the deployment window — blue/green was mis-tagged so both wrote to the same export prefix. Result: schema drift mid-export.

jason (eng-security): Splunk props at the customer expects `actor_id` (snake_case). Mixed events will cause their ingestion pipeline to reject per their strict schema. Two remediation paths: a) re-run export converting all event keys to snake_case for that window and re-deliver; b) provide field aliasing/props update on their Splunk side. Customer wants us to re-stream the normalized artifacts.

maya (support): They prefer we re-send. They also flagged the `403 kms decrypt` on 4 objects — they can't ingest those.

nate (sre): For the kms failures, the export manifest shows object metadata `x-amz-meta-kms-key: null` on 4 gz files. I'll pull logs to see if exporter failed to attach kms_key_id for certain shards. If those objects are encrypted with a different key, SIEM won't decrypt.

emily (infra): Found root cause for kms: exporter had a race in obtaining temporary grants from our KMS proxy — grant id lookup returned null for some shards due to token expiry in the retrier. We'll backfill those four objects by re-encrypting with the expected key and re-uploading.

jason (eng-security): Action list:
- nate to re-run export job for `2026-03-05` with canonical snake_case normalization and upload to `s3://redwood-audit-prod/exports/2026-03-05/reprocessed/` (ETA 4h) — @nate
- emily to backfill/re-encrypt the 4 kms-skipped objects and mark them present in the manifest (ETA 2h) — @emily
- claire/maya to coordinate re-ingest with Acme and confirm Splunk props; provide sample transformed file for validation (ETA 1h) — @claire
- jason to file a postmortem and set exporter canary to prevent mixed-version writes (ETA EOD) — @jason

claire (support): I'll send an example of the reprocessed file to Acme SRE right away, and ask them to temporarily accept `actorId` aliases while we reprocess.

maya (support): Acme acknowledged and asked for a checksum of the reprocessed file and a replay token so they can dedupe — I'll get that from Nate once ready.

nate (sre): Starting reprocess now. Command I'm running: `./export-tool --job export-job-20260305-42 --normalize snake_case --output s3://redwood-audit-prod/exports/2026-03-05/reprocessed/` Will attach checksum when done.

audits-bot: reprocess export-job-20260305-42 started at 2026-03-06T09:12:30Z, task_id: `rpr-77c9`

jason (eng-security): Thanks team. Claire/maya — please hold the customer on a short maintenance window for re-ingest. I'll own the postmortem and follow up on exporter version pinning. :thumbsup:

claire (support): Noted. Posting an update to the customer in the ticket now.

maya (support): I'll keep this thread updated with re-ingest confirmation and checksum.

(THREAD END)
